title: Predicting the experimental lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
description:
A curated, provenance-tracked corpus of half-Heusler lattice thermal conductivity in which laboratory measurements and first-principles transport calculations are tiered separately and never pooled, with the code for a two-step prediction: a machine-learned model that predicts the Boltzmann-transport value from crystal structure, and a two-parameter transfer function that maps a calculation onto the experimental scale.

Published transport calculations exceed measured half-Heusler lattice thermal conductivity by a median factor of 1.69 (34 compounds). The model reproduces published calculations to a median error of 21.9 %. Holding each compound's chemistry cluster out of both steps, inside a predefined domain of applicability, the median error against measurement is 33.1 % and 87.2 % of 39 compounds lie within a factor of two (median of five model seeds); without the domain screens, all 50 measured compounds give 38.6 % and 78.9 %.

The archive contains the curated corpus, the prediction list with its refusals, the five model seeds behind every seed-averaged figure, and the code that regenerates every figure and number in the paper. Code is MIT licensed; the curated data are CC BY 4.0. Upstream databases (Starrydata2, AFLOW, Materials Project, JARVIS, OQMD, COD) are fetched by the scripts rather than redistributed here — see LICENSE-DATA.
